title: Dam Good Maps collaboration session v1
description: The messages two players' sessions exchange besides the ordered log's own (collab.schema.json): joining (hello, welcome, ready), claims ordered through the host, desync reports, leaving and presence. Each definition is one message; wire.ts picks one by its "kind" and refuses anything else with one line. The map's project bytes travel as the binary message that follows a welcome. Version 1; a hello or welcome with another version is refused as incompatible.

name.description: A player's display name, set by the player.

hello.description: The guest to the host, as soon as the connection is up (a joiner or a rejoiner alike).

welcome.description: The host to the guest, answering a hello or a resync: the session, both names, the map's snapshot header (its project bytes are the next message) and the claims as they stand.

ready.description: The guest to the host: the snapshot is adopted and this copy matches the host's at that moment.

claim.description: The guest to the host: a claims command (claims.schema.json), ordered by the host with the log.

claims.description: The host to everyone: a claims command that stood, in its place among the entries. `by` gave it; `revision` is the claims' revision after it (a peer that differs is out of step).

claimReject.description: The host to the guest: a claims command that was refused, with one plain reason.

desync.description: Either side: this copy of the map differs from the host's (the replica found it); the other side is told so both pages can say so.

resync.description: The guest to the host: send the map again (after a desync).

bye.description: Either side: leaving on purpose, so the other's page says so at once.

presence.description: Where a player is and what they are doing, on the unordered channel at up to 15 per second (the latest wins), and a stroke's start and end also on the ordered one. Cursor and stroke points are quarter-tile integers (null hides the cursor); the stroke is an id, a part number and a bounded run of points since the last packet; view is the camera (target, distance, yaw, pitch). Name and colour are the session's, never sent here. Nothing in it edits the map.
